parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the period of a pendulum. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 1.1 and Fig. 1.2. Fig. 1.1 Fig. 1.2 A pendulum has been set up for you as shown in Fig. 1.1.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Measure the distance l between the bottom of the clamp supporting the pendulum and the centre of the pendulum bob. l = ................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 1(a)(i)
ms.text: l = 35.0 cm – 45.0 cm given to nearest mm

ms.label: 1(a)(ii)
ms.text: Clear use of horizontal aid OR bob touching rule

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Adjust the length of the pendulum until the distance l = 50.0 cm. Displace the bob slightly and release it so that it swings. Fig. 1.2 shows one complete oscillation of the pendulum. Measure, and record in Table 1.1, the time t for 20 complete oscillations. Calculate, and record in Table 1.1, the period T of the pendulum. The period is the time for one complete oscillation. Calculate, and record in Table 1.1, the value of T 2 . Repeat the procedure using l values of 60.0 cm, 70.0 cm, 80.0 cm and 90.0 cm. Table 1.1 l / cm t / s T / s T 2 / s 2 50.0 60.0 70.0 80.0 90.0 [4]

ms.text:

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of T 2 / s 2 ( y -axis) against l / cm ( x -axis). Start the T 2 axis at a convenient value close to the minimum value of T 2 . [4]
